feature: Letting a colour go on a part that is switched off
summary: A colour can now be dropped on the Outline, Fill or Shadow row of a layer that has none. The part comes on wearing that colour, in one step one undo puts back. Before, those rows refused the colour and the only way to a coloured edge was to find the switch, flip it, and repaint whatever came back.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing to switch on: this rides on the Appearance list and colour dragging, both already on.

try.do: Draw a rectangle, then click it with the arrow tool.
In Appearance, click the Outline switch to take the line off.
Press and hold the Fill swatch, then drag it left onto the word Outline.
Let go. The outline comes on wearing the fill colour, with its Width row under it.
Press Command Z once and check the whole thing goes back, colour and line together.
Drag the Fill swatch onto the Shadow row and let go.
Drag a saved colour off the Library shelf onto a switched-off Outline row.

evaluate: When you are holding a colour over an off row, does the ring plus the swatch appearing in the colour column make it obvious what letting go will do?
Is aiming at the whole row easier than aiming at a swatch would have been?
Does one undo taking back both the line and the colour feel right, or would you rather undo the colour and keep the line?
The row still shows nothing at rest. Is a name and an off switch enough to tell you the part is absent, or do you want the colour it would come back at showing there?
Should the same drop work on the Shadow row, or is a shadow different enough that it should stay switch-first?
rough: The row shows nothing at rest, on purpose: the Appearance list is built on off looking off. So this gesture is not discoverable by looking. It only helps someone already carrying a colour, which is the case that used to be refused. If you want off rows to advertise a colour, that is a different and bigger change.
Dropping on a mixed row (one box outlined, one not) gives all of them the line in that colour, matching what the switch already does. It has core tests but no walk.
The Fill row taking a drop while it is off has core tests but is not in the walk either; only Outline and Shadow are walked.

The queued task also asked whether a freshly drawn rectangle has no outline. It does have one: the default is a 4 pt stroke. The bare box in the task's evidence came from the panel arming the tool, which is deliberate, so nothing was changed there.
Screen Recording was granted, so every picture here is a real window capture, not an offscreen render.
